text.text: Payment-service is failing payments due to PostgreSQL connection timeouts and pool exhaustion (`DB_CONN_TIMEOUT`, `PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved`), and it is also crashing with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` and `OOMKilled` in CrashLoopBackOff. Postgres-primary is under contention with `active_connections=195/200`, `slow_query_ms=8421`, and `lock_wait_ms=6032`, while auth-service and api-gateway are also returning 401s from Redis session lookup timeouts. Overall severity is P1, with immediate user impact on payment submission and authentication-dependent API access, and the recent payment-service v2.8.4 deployment has only 1/6 replicas available. The single most critical next step is to roll back payment-service from v2.8.4 to v2.8.3 and pause the rollout while relieving postgres-primary connection pressure.

*Issues Identified:*
• *DB_TIMEOUT* on `payment-service, postgres-primary, api-gateway` — P1 (confidence: 99%)
• *OOM_KILL* on `payment-service, kubelet, kubernetes` — P1 (confidence: 99%)
• *DB_TIMEOUT* on `postgres-primary, payment-service` — P1 (confidence: 94%)
• *AUTH_ERROR* on `auth-service, redis-cache, api-gateway` — P1 (confidence: 98%)
• *DEPLOY_FAILURE* on `payment-service, deployment-controller, kubernetes` — P2 (confidence: 82%)
